newsitem.title: USA: Shell, Texaco confirm talks on linkup.
newsitem.headline: Shell, Texaco confirm talks on linkup.

text.p: Oil giants Texaco Inc. and Shell Oil Co. said Monday they were in talks over a potential linkup of their refining and marketing operations in the United States.

"Shell Oil Company confirms it is discussing with Texaco the potential for joint arrangements involving U.S. downstream operations," Shell said in a statement. "While the companies are reviewing a range of options concerning the businesses that might be included, no decisions have been made."
Texaco also confirmed it was in discussions about a potential alliance.
It said the goal of the talks was to create a more efficient competitive operation maximizing the strengths of both companies, including their individual brands.
Word of the talks follows an agreement earlier his year between Mobil Corp. and British Petroleum Plc to merge their refining and markleting operations in Europe.
The moves are part of a trend in the oil industry to cut costs and increase efficiencies in the face of dwindling profit margins.

The companies' statements were in response to a Wall Street Journal report Monday that said Shell, Texaco and state-owned Saudi Aramco were in talks over a possible three-way merger that would pool assets valued at more than $10 billion.

The newspaper said the merger would combine the "downstream forces" of Texaco, Shell, the U.S. unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, and Star Enterprise, a joint venture between Texaco and Saudi Aramco, the state oil company of Saudi Arabia.
It cited people close to the negotiations as its source of information.
The newspaper said the new companies would control about 15 percent of the petroleum-products market in the United States.
The talks were being guided by CS First Boston Corp. for Texaco, Morgan Stanley Group Inc.'s Morgan Stanley & Co. unit for Shell and J.P. Morgan & Co. for Star, the newspaper said.
